rounds.text: Current Infraprojects Ltd is deeply under-appreciated by the market, trading at a modest P/E of 12.6x while delivering elite profitability metrics that thoroughly outpace its sector benchmarks [E1, E8, E9, E10]. Specifically, the company generates an exceptional Return on Equity (ROE) of 27.17% and Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) of 25.74%, compared to sector benchmarks of just 10.51% and 12.7% respectively [E9, E10]. This fundamental business strength is matched by explosive top and bottom-line expansion, with trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth surging at 88% and compounded profit growth reaching 62% [E14, E15]. Operating margins are also expanding powerfully, climbing to 15% in the trailing twelve months from 11% three years prior, and further accelerating to 19% in the September 2026 quarter [E18, E19]. Despite these stellar fundamental improvements and a high rules-based screen score of 78 out of 100, the stock has suffered a 35% decline over the past year, leaving it disconnected from its fundamental momentum and sitting only 34% of the way up its 52-week range [E5, E16, E40]. Conceded: the company carries negative operating and free cash flows for March 2026 alongside a 0.00% dividend yield [E4, E23, E24].

Conceded: [E14], [E15]. Despite impressive reported sales growth of 88% and profit growth of 62% over the trailing twelve months, the company's share price has plummeted 35% over the past year [E14, E15, E16]. This sharp divergence highlights severe market skepticism regarding the quality and durability of these reported earnings. The core concern is that reported profits are entirely disconnected from actual cash generation, as evidenced by a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -0.64x for March 2026 [E22]. Operating cash flow stands at a negative Rs 9 Cr alongside a staggering free cash flow burn of Rs 30 Cr in March 2026 [E23, E24]. Compounding these liquidity strains, total borrowings have escalated to Rs 49 Cr in September 2026, rising significantly from Rs 33 Cr a year prior [E27]. Furthermore, foreign institutional investors have trimmed their holdings down to 3.98% from 7.32% over the same period, signaling a flight of sophisticated capital [E30].

Conceded: [E22], [E23], [E24], [E27], [E30]. While cash generation and borrowings require monitoring and FIIs reduced their stake [E22, E23, E24, E27, E30], the bear misreads the valuation disconnect; the market price of Rs 100 sits at a modest P/E of 12.6x [E1, E2] with a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 179 [E33], leaving a massive 44% margin of safety [E34]. The market's 35% share price drop over the past year [E16] clashes directly with surging fundamentals—namely 88% sales growth and 62% profit growth [E14, E15]—creating a classic sentiment lag where profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 97% [E37]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's depressed price prices in a meager 1.9% earnings growth against a 10.0% base case [E35], meaning expectations are set impossibly low for a company delivering elite efficiency metrics like a 27.2% ROCE [E12]. Institutional confidence is actually strengthening overall, demonstrated by domestic institutions increasing their holdings to 10.81% [E31] and positive money flow signals [E32], while operating margins expand to 19% in the recent quarter [E19].

Conceded: [E31], [E32], [E35]. The bull's reliance on a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 179 [E33] and a 44% margin of safety [E34] is severely undermined by a complete collapse in cash generation, evidenced by negative operating cash flow of Rs -9 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -30 Cr for Mar 2026 [E23, E24]. While the bull highlights surging sales and profit growth [E14, E15], this paper-profit expansion has failed to materialize into actual liquidity, resulting in a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -0.64x [E22] and rising borrowings that jumped to Rs 49 Cr in Sep 2026 from Rs 33 Cr a year prior [E27]. Furthermore, the bull's narrative of strong market support is contradicted by foreign institutional investors slashing their holdings from 7.32% to 3.98% [E30] and a 35% crash in the share price over the past year [E16]. The company's operating-margin trend is explicitly flagged as inconsistent across both yearly and quarterly horizons [E20, E21], and management retains zero dividend payout despite reporting profits [E39], signaling that reported earnings do not safely reach shareholders.
